artifacts.summary: Per-phase record of the seven-phase implementation, its verification counts, plan deviations, and the deferred stash drop.
The recommendation document: ILMC named, measurement tables citing tests and baselines, Concessions and Further Tests sections.
Six candidate Z3 operators (I, ILC, ILMC, W, L, MC) plus might variants sharing the truth clause verbatim.

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented and measured the candidate verifier clauses for the logos counterfactual: recovered the stashed Z3 substrate, ported every research clause and witness frame into the committed oracle with pinned characterization tests, added ILC/ILMC/MC as Z3 operators cross-validated against the oracle, built nested-antecedent and constitutive example collections with Z3 confirmation, and delivered the recommendation report naming ILMC (exact settled-imposition verifiers) with its concessions. Along the way fixed a pre-existing bound-variable capture in CounterfactualOperator.true_at/false_at and established, against the research's small-frame hypothesis, that ILMC/ILC are hyperintensional on possible states already at four atoms (Z3-confirmed at N=4).

memory_candidates.content: model_checker.utils.ForAll/Exists expand quantifiers by substituting for a NAMED z3 constant. Any operator whose true_at/false_at creates bound variables with a fixed name (e.g. z3.BitVec('t_cf_u', N)) and passes that bound variable as the evaluation world to a nested occurrence of the same operator suffers variable capture: the inner expansion substitutes the outer's bound world too, and the inner clause loses its evaluation world entirely. Fix: draw fresh names per call (itertools.count suffix). Probe: build sem.true_at(inner, {'world': z3.BitVec('probe', N)}) and check the expression still mentions 'probe'. imposition/operators.py still has the fixed-name pattern.

Oracle-first measurement pattern for semantic clause exploration: state every candidate clause over explicit finite frames in pure Python (bitmask states), pin counts as characterization tests on seeded/exhaustive populations, then confirm with Z3 at small N via cross-validation (Python side == oracle on the extracted frame == Z3 clause at every state and evaluation world). Sampling zeros are not coincidence proofs: a 300-model sample at n=4 missed separations that a 20,000-model sample and Z3's exhaustive search both found; scale the sample or ask Z3 before declaring two clauses coincide.

For Z3 clauses with several quantifier layers over concrete states (fusion closure, minimality, settling, imposition), iterate concrete states in Python and memoize each per-state subterm on the semantics instance keyed by (clause, argument names, state, encoding). Shared DAG subterms keep a four-layer clause (ILMC) at ~1 s for N=4; an unmemoized settler term made one cross-validation test take 27 s.

reflection.what_worked: Recovering the stashed substrate by explicit path and running the full suite immediately surfaced the capture defect before any new clause depended on it; the oracle-first split let every structural and logical claim be pinned in seconds and left Z3 only the confirmation role.
reflection.what_was_hard: Interpreting the N=4 constitutive countermodels: Z3's returned models separated the pair only on impossible states, so it took large oracle samples and a Z3 seed sweep to establish that possible-state separations exist at four atoms too.
reflection.what_was_missed: The plan assumed the tree would be clean for the stash drop; inside an orchestrated dispatch the orchestrator's own lock and event files keep it dirty, so that step had to be recorded as a reasoned exclusion rather than executed.
reflection.successes: All seven phases closed with green gates (logos 747, code/tests 680); the recommendation is backed by pinned tests and ten baselines, and two research claims were corrected by measurement (the SR/SRC count and the small-frame-coincidence reading).

next_steps: Drop stash@{0} on a clean tree (redundant with commit 64eb483b) and remove .git-snapshot-marker and working-progress-1788911805.patch; consider follow-up tasks for adopting \boxrightILMC as the successor operator and for the same bound-variable fix in imposition/operators.py.
